general.title: General Settings
general.content:
• 📊 Set your organization/site name (used in schema and social sharing)
  • 🖼️ Upload a logo for previews and schema (square or wide both work)
  • 💡 Keep your site name and logo consistent everywhere
  • ℹ️ These settings improve clarity, not rankings

verification.title: Search Engine Verification
verification.content:
• 🔑 Verification proves that you own this website
  • 📊 It allows search engines to show you reports about your site
  • 🔍 Google Search Console shows indexing, errors, and search traffic
  • 🌐 Bing Webmaster Tools shows crawl and visibility data for Bing
  • 🧭 Yandex is useful only if you target Russian or CIS regions
  • ✂️ Paste only the content value — the plugin adds the full meta tag automatically
  • ⚠️ Verification does not improve rankings by itself
  • ℹ️ After saving, complete verification inside each webmaster tool

indexnow.title: IndexNow (Instant URL Notification)
indexnow.content:
• 🚀 IndexNow notifies participating search engines when a page is added, updated, or removed
  • 🌐 Supported by Bing, Yandex, Seznam, and other IndexNow partners
  • ❌ Google does not currently use IndexNow
  • 🔄 Pages may still take time to appear — indexing is not guaranteed
  • 🔑 The API key is generated automatically and identifies your site
  • ⏱️ Most useful for frequently updated or time-sensitive content
  • ℹ️ This feature improves discovery speed, not rankings

social.title: Social Sharing (Open Graph & Twitter)
social.content:
• 🖼️ Controls how your pages look when shared on social apps
  • 📌 A default image is used when a page has no featured image
  • 📏 Recommended image size: 1200×630 pixels (works on most platforms)
  • 🌐 Most platforms use Open Graph tags automatically
  • 🐦 Twitter/X uses its own card format for large preview images
  • 📘 Facebook App ID is optional and used only for Insights and validation
  • 🎨 Theme color affects link previews in some apps (Discord, Telegram)
  • ℹ️ Social tags affect previews — not Google rankings

schema.title: Schema (Structured Data)
schema.content:
• 🏷️ Schema adds structured information so search engines understand your site
  • 📄 It describes what your pages represent (organization, business, breadcrumbs)
  • ✨ Some schema types may be used for rich results if search engines choose to
  • 🏢 Enable Local Business only if you serve customers in a physical or service area
  • 📍 Business details should exactly match your Google Business Profile
  • 🧭 Breadcrumbs help search engines understand page hierarchy
  • ⚠️ Schema improves clarity — rich results and rankings are never guaranteed
  • ℹ️ Leaving optional fields empty will not harm your site

templates.title: SEO Templates (Automatic Fallbacks)
templates.content:
• 🧩 Templates are used only when a page does not have custom SEO values
  • ✏️ Page-level titles and descriptions always take priority
  • 🏷️ Use variables to create consistent, readable fallbacks
  • ➗ The separator controls how titles are visually split
  • 🧠 Simple templates are usually better than complex ones
  • 📄 Descriptions can be left empty to auto-generate from content
  • ℹ️ Templates help consistency — they do not guarantee rankings

maintenance.title: Safety & Maintenance
maintenance.content:
• 🛠️ This page is for maintenance and recovery — most users rarely need it
  • 📦 Export settings before making major changes or updates
  • 📥 Import settings only from files created by this plugin
  • 🔄 Reset removes all plugin settings and cannot be undone
  • 🧪 Use reset only for troubleshooting or starting fresh
  • ⚠️ These tools do not affect rankings directly

cards.title: About Page Diagnostics
cards.content: Inspect a single page and see exactly what search engines can read from it — including title, description, canonical URL, indexing rules, and structured data.

cards.title: How to Use
cards.content:
• Select a page from your site or paste a full URL
  • Click Run Diagnostics to fetch the page
  • Review each section to confirm what search engines and social platforms can read
  • Tip: This tool does not change your page — it only inspects it

cards.title: What You’ll See
cards.content:
• Page Fetch: Whether the page loads correctly or redirects
  • Indexing Rules: Whether the page is allowed to appear in search results
  • Canonical URL: Which URL the page declares as its main version
  • Meta & Schema: Title, description, social preview tags, and structured data

cards.title: Note
cards.content: This page is read-only. It shows factual output only — no scoring, no recommendations, and no ranking predictions. Use it to spot missing, conflicting, or unexpected signals.

cards.title: About Site Diagnostics
cards.content:
Site Diagnostics checks site-wide SEO patterns that may affect how search engines discover, understand, and index your pages. It focuses on global signals, not individual pages.

This helps you identify issues that impact all pages at once.

cards.title: Can search engines easily discover your pages?
cards.content:
• Checks whether your XML sitemap exists and is accessible
  • Verifies HTTP status of the sitemap
  • Confirms whether the sitemap is referenced in robots.txt
  • Shows whether WordPress is managing the sitemap

Why this matters: If search engines cannot find your sitemap, they may discover pages slowly or miss updates.

cards.title: Is your site sending clear, single signals?
cards.content:
• Detects multiple active SEO plugins
  • Checks for duplicate title tags
  • Checks for duplicate meta descriptions
  • Verifies single canonical output
  • Ensures robots and schema tags are not duplicated

Why this matters: Search engines expect one clear SEO signal per page. Multiple outputs can cause confusion.

cards.title: Is anything blocking your site from search results?
cards.content:
• Checks if global noindex is enabled
  • Detects large robots.txt crawl blocks
  • Reviews sitemap accessibility
  • Samples redirect chains that may block crawling

Important: Even a well-optimized site cannot appear in search results if indexing is blocked.

cards.title: Do pages clearly identify their main URL?
cards.content:
• Detects pages canonicalizing to the homepage
  • Checks for canonical loops
  • Finds canonicals pointing to redirected URLs
  • Verifies consistent HTTP / HTTPS usage
  • Confirms default WordPress canonical behavior

Why this matters: Canonical URLs tell search engines which version of a page should be indexed.

cards.title: How to use this page
cards.content:
1. Fix blocking issues (red status) first
  2. Resolve duplicate or conflict warnings next
  3. Use Page Diagnostics for deep checks on individual URLs
  4. Re-run Site Diagnostics after major changes

cards.title: Important Note
cards.content:
This page shows facts and detected patterns only.

It does not predict rankings, assign scores, or guarantee results. It reflects what search engines can see at a site-wide level.

cards.title: About SEO Bulk Edit
cards.content:
Bulk Edit lets you update SEO titles, descriptions, and indexing settings for multiple posts at once.

This is useful when cleaning up old content or applying consistent SEO rules.

cards.title: How to use Bulk Edit
cards.content:
• Filter by post type (Posts, Pages, etc.)
  • Optionally filter by indexing status
  • Select the items you want to change
  • Apply a bulk action or edit fields inline

cards.title: Bulk actions explained
cards.content:
• Set to Index: Allow selected pages to appear in search results
  • Set to Noindex: Prevent selected pages from appearing in search results
  • Clear SEO Titles: Revert to automatic title generation
  • Clear Descriptions: Allow descriptions to be auto-generated

cards.title: Best practices
cards.content:
• Make small, controlled changes
  • Avoid using the same title across many pages
  • Use Noindex carefully — it removes pages from search results
  • Review a few updated pages in Page Diagnostics after saving

cards.title: Important notes
cards.content:
• Changes are applied only after clicking Save All Changes
  • Bulk edits affect many pages — double-check selections
  • This tool does not change content, only SEO metadata

cards.title: About SEO Redirects
cards.content:
Redirects guide visitors and search engines from an old URL to the correct page when URLs change.

This helps avoid broken links and preserves search visibility.

cards.title: How redirects work
cards.content:
• Visitors are automatically sent from the old URL to the new one
  • Search engines update their records over time
  • The original URL does not show content anymore

Why this matters: Without redirects, users may see errors and search engines may drop old pages.

cards.title: Choosing the right redirect type
cards.content:
• 301 (Permanent): Use when a page has moved permanently (recommended for SEO)
  • 302 / 307 (Temporary): Use when the change is short-term and the original page will return

Tip: Temporary redirects keep the original URL indexed.

cards.title: Best practices
cards.content:
• Always test the old URL after adding a redirect
  • Avoid redirect chains (URL A → B → C)
  • Remove redirects that are no longer needed
  • Use relative paths when redirecting within the same site

cards.title: Important Note
cards.content:
This tool manages redirects only.

It does not modify page content, predict rankings, or guarantee SEO improvements.

cards.title: About robots.txt
cards.content:
The robots.txt file tells search engines which parts of your site they are allowed to visit.

It controls crawling only — not rankings or indexing.

cards.title: What robots.txt does (and doesn’t do)
cards.content:
• Controls which URLs search engines can crawl
  • Does not control rankings
  • Does not hide pages from the public

Important: Pages blocked here may still appear in search results if linked elsewhere.

cards.title: Common safe rules
cards.content:
• Block /wp-admin/ except admin-ajax.php
  • Block /wp-includes/ system files
  • Allow all public content
  • Include your sitemap URL

These defaults are safe for most WordPress sites.

cards.title: When to be careful
cards.content:
• Do not block CSS or JavaScript needed for page rendering
  • Do not use robots.txt to hide sensitive or private content
  • Avoid blocking entire sections unless necessary

Incorrect rules can prevent search engines from understanding your pages.

cards.title: After making changes
cards.content:
• Save the file and view the live robots.txt
  • Test important pages using Page Diagnostics
  • Re-check crawling status in Google Search Console
